utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Good afternoon to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, I'm Tom Hannis, along with Gramsci Di Fazio and Crispian Smith for the Prosecution. We do have a couple of preliminary matters we'd like to raise before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Dragan Krgovic and Igor Pantelic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio has a matter concerning the witness. I have two other matters I was asked to bring to your attention. One is Mr. Olmsted has a witness scheduled to begin testifying next week on Wednesday the 25th, it's ST-210. There's pending a motion from the Prosecution to change his mode of testimony from viva voce to 92 ter. I think the Defence had filed a response today. And we would ask your ruling on that at the earliest possible date so Mr. Olmsted can plan accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. And the second one is Ms. Korner has pending -- well, we have pending a motion to add an exhibit. It's a video to be used with Witness ST-23 who will be testifying on Monday, the 30th of August. That's all I had. Mr. Di Fazio, I think, and Mr. Zecevic have something to discuss concerning today's witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't know if Your Honours want to hear from the Defence first, but let me outline basically what the problem is. The witness who's about to testify, Mr. Tihic, wrote a set of memoirs. They consist of about 66 pages of B/C/S typed memoirs, and they were not disclosed to the Defence until earlier today, not long ago. I can give you an explanation of why or how this happened, and I accept -- I must accept full responsibility for this error and I do. The Defence -- some of the Defence lawyers are not entirely unfamiliar with this document, in particular Mr. Zecevic and Mr. Pantelic. It's referred to in the cross-examination of this witness from the Simic case, the testimony that we would hope eventually to tender into evidence in this particular case. The document is referred there. However, that being said, it doesn't change the fact that in this particular case we did not disclose the memoirs until just a short while ago. Accordingly, I don't know what the attitude of the Defence is to this situation. I understand that the Defence would be willing to go as far as they can with cross-examination and would then require some time to look at the memoirs in order to be able to complete their cross-examination. I understand that that's the situation. And I'm sure that Mr. Zecevic can enlighten you further on that. The witness himself is here, is available, and would be available tomorrow, but would have troubles returning -- in fact, can't return next week and is heavily booked because of his -- he's a politician, of course, and -- a high-ranking politician in Bosnia and is going to have trouble getting back in the near future. So certainly he can finish his evidence tomorrow. He can remain here overnight, and that's not a problem for him. I've already discussed that with him. So I would ask if the Defence can enlighten the Trial Chamber as to what consequences this has for them. I would hope that we can proceed as far as we can today and that a short break today or overnight would enable them to be able to complete their cross-examination. And, of course, everything I say is subject to the Trial Chamber's availability. I'm mindful of that. I'm not ignoring that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, about overbooking or heavily booking, how are we booked for next week?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't have the trial -- the schedule of witnesses at my finger-tips. I can certainly find out immediately -- fairly quickly for you. If you give me a moment, I'll make inquiries and see what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I will speak in Serbian. [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is a fact that at 12.30 today we received that statement which in the course of this witness's testimony in the Seselj case was extensively used. I was truly unable in such a short time to go through the statement, those memoirs, or the things that the witness can remember that are contained in the statement. I seem to recall somewhat parts of those documents from back in 2001, but since I haven't seen those documents for almost a decade now, including the period when we were preparing for the cross-examination of this witness, I'm truly unable to rely on my recollection only. I would truly need to read the document first. I would much prefer if in any way possible that my cross-examination not be interrupted, since what I intended originally to ask the witness could be changed based on what I find in the document that was disclosed to me at half past noon. During an informal conversation we had before the hearing, I realised that there are some problems in that regard. I'm of course willing to accept any ruling on your part. I'm merely expressing my preference. Our clients, however, informed us that they also relied on this Friday being a free day because they wanted to enjoy some of the activities which they otherwise cannot when we sit in the afternoon. I believe you're all aware of that. Having in mind the needs of the Chamber, however, I will follow your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, the -- before I hear -- I see Mr. Pantelic is on his feet, but two questions before I give the floor to Mr. Pantelic. We have noted your preference, but it would probably, in terms of the efficient management of our time -- we would probably require you to at least begin. But I do have a concern as to whether -- if we do sit in the morning, whether you expect that you would -- and I know this is a somewhat difficult question to -- for you to respond to at this point, not having digested the documents, but do you reasonably anticipate that with the Court sitting tomorrow morning with a view to completing this witness -- because we keep in mind the time constraints of the witness, whether you expect that you would be -- whether you could finish tomorrow morning?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And we would -- we would adjourn earlier today in any event because we appreciate that we would -- you would need time to deal with this. But do you expect you could finish tomorrow? That's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I -- Your Honours, thank you very much for your full understanding of my situation. But I do reasonably anticipate that I would be able to analyse and read the document overnight and be prepared for a cross-examination tomorrow. And I will finish definitely with the witness. What I'm -- what I -- what my concern is is that I might -- I reserved three hours for cross-examination -- or estimated three hours for cross-examination of this witness. However, I might be much shorter if I would be able to have the whole picture. I would have -- probably be shorter than three hours. But I -- that is the part I cannot guarantee. Now, in this way, I might be repeating myself and posing the questions to the witness twice, today and tomorrow. But if that is the preference of the Trial Chamber, I'm -- as I said, I'm perfectly willing to adhere to that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I will be brief. I just want to say something for the record. This specific witness does not testify to the municipality that is part of the indictment against my client. We may have a few questions, which is not the crucial point in this point in time. Since my learned friend Mr. Di Fazio mentioned that I was probably familiar with these documents, I can only state for the record that a decade later I have no clue what is in the document, as opposed to the -- most of the witnesses of the Prosecution who seem to have a fantastic memory, even 20 years down the road. As opposed to that, I'm afraid my memory is not as good.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Before we rule on this matter, the -- we are reminded of what Mr. Zecevic has indicated as to the position of the accused themselves, and the -- it would be helpful to us if counsel -- well, counsel of course always speak on behalf of their clients, but with this latest development of which the accused would have just become aware, if perhaps both counsel could consult sotto voce with their clients and then let the Chamber know whether -- whether the accused would be willing to come in for a short period tomorrow -- tomorrow morning, a morning session, in order to complete this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Shall we do that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- right now in the courtroom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm suggesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have consulted our clients. The problem was that Mr. Zupljanin has a religious ceremony scheduled earlier in the morning, and just prior to that we had planned to visit them at 10.00 in the Detention Unit. We will try to reshuffle that, but first we need to see with Mr. Zupljanin whether he can reschedule as well for the afternoon. In that case, I believe we could sit for a shorter period of time in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course -- Mr. Krgovic, of course -- and Mr. Zecevic, the -- of course the -- your clients are aware that they may decline to be present. But, Mr. Zecevic, what is your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, my client's position is that he doesn't want to waive his right to be present because this is one of the witnesses from the municipality that he is charged with. But understanding the difficulty which the Trial Chamber is experiencing due to this unfortunate situation, he's, of course, accepting to come tomorrow, as is Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So both clients are basically understanding the situation. They will appear tomorrow in the court. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Di Fazio, anything further on this issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Only to say that I'm extremely grateful to Defence counsel for -- and the Trial Chamber for your understanding in this situation. I must accept full responsibility for this. And I hope that the arrangements will rectify my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. So the usher would escort --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, and on -- we have witnesses for Monday. I just want to make sure that we don't have a blank hearing on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, no, we're full next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: We're fully booked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Fully booked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Witness. First of all, do you hear me in a language you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give your testimony. You're about to read the solemn declaration by which witnesses commit themselves to tell the truth. I need to point out that the solemn declaration that you are about to make does expose you to the penalties of perjury should you give misleading or untruthful evidence to this Tribunal. Now then, would you please be kind enough to read aloud the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You may be seated. And, sir, could you -- could we begin by asking you to state your full name and full date of and place of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Sulejman Tihic. I was born on the 26th of November, 1951, in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Your profession today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My profession is -- well, I'm currently the deputy presiding officer of the house of the peoples of the Bosnia-Herzegovina parliament.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And what was your occupation in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was an attorney-at-law in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, is this your first testimony before this Tribunal, or have you ever testified in any domestic criminal procedure about these matters, about the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have testified several times before this Tribunal in various cases, such as Tadic, Simic, Seselj, Milosevic, Simatovic, Stanisic, and this one of course. I have not testified on these matters before any domestic courts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That means that you know how things work here, I suppose. You know that you will be asked, first, questions by the Prosecutor, who called you as a witness; then there is a cross-examination; and a re-examination; and eventually the Judges will have questions of you. You probably remember that these sessions take half a day, in the afternoon from 2.15 till 7.00. If it is in the -- a morning session, which will probably be the case tomorrow, it would be from 9.00 to quarter to 2.00. And that these -- that there are pauses every -- more or less every 90 minutes for technical reasons. However, if for any other reason you personally need a short break, please let us know and we will accommodate you. That's all I have to say. Thank you very much. And I will give the floor to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Sir, you just mentioned moments ago that you had testified in the Stanisic and Simatovic case. Did that take place in February of this year?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the course of preparing for that testimony in that case, in Stanisic and Simatovic, did you have occasion to review your testimony in the Simic case which you gave in September and November of 2001?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. It was quite a voluminous testimony which comprised, I believe, a few hundred pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, you have my sympathies. Having reviewed that testimony in February of this year, are you able to affirm the accuracy and truthfulness of that testimony?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions today, would you provide the same answers and evidence?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if Your Honours please, I'll be seeking the usual orders, eventually.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In the Simic case, you described quite detailed your education and the work that you'd been doing -- the sort of work you'd been doing as a lawyer in Bosanski Samac right up -- up to 1992, and then you also described your developing political career after 1992. And you described it right up until 2001. And again this morning you just told the Trial Chamber that your position currently is that of deputy president of the BiH Bosnian parliament. I'd like you to fill in for the Trial Chamber, please, your career between 2001 and the present time in a fairly broad outline. Just give the Trial Chamber a picture of what you've been doing, in effect, in the last decade.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: In 2001, I was elected president of the SDA party. In -- and I'm still in that position. And I've been elected so far in three party congresses. 2002, I was elected member of the Bosnia-Herzegovina Presidency. In 2007, I was elected deputy speaker of the house of the peoples of the Bosnia-Herzegovina parliament. People rotate in that function, taking turns every eight months.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And that's the position you continue to hold today?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. In your evidence from Simic, it's quite clear that you are Bosanski Samac born and bred and you described -- you still have continuing relations with the city and you go back there and you have familiar there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. My family -- my extended family live in Bosanski Samac. My granddaughters live there, they attend school there. And I go there every other weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to begin by showing you some maps, if I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown 65 ter 10470.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, is that a map of Bosanski Samac and the Sava River and surrounding towns and villages?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. There's -- two places in red are mentioned. Firstly, if I may deal with one, Batkusa. In your evidence, you described paramilitaries being flown -- arriving in Batkusa in a helicopter about 11 or so days prior to the take-over in April in 1992. Is that where the -- they were flying to, that place indicated there in red, Batkusa?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was told by -- this by a client of mine, when I was an attorney, that there were some helicopters who landed there in Batkusa from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. But that place -- we've got all your evidence concerning that, thank you. But that place there in red lettering in the map saying "Batkusa," that's the place that you understand they landed at?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you describe in your evidence the notorious man, the well-known man, Mr. -- nicknamed Lugar Slobodan Miljkovic. And I -- it's not in -- it can't be in dispute that he was involved in a massacre of people at Crkvina. Do you see the place called Crkvina in red bold in the map?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you're talking about the massacre that was in May 1992; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. And the place marked in red in bold on this map that you see in front of you, that's the same Crkvina that you're talking about, the place that Lugar carried out his massacre?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. About how far is Crkvina from Bosanski Samac, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Five kilometres, five to six.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I tender the map, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P01544, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can I just show you another map, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: 65 ter number 10469, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that a map of -- a more detailed map of the township of Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I may need the assistance of the usher. I'm going to ask that the map be marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You gave extensive evidence in the Simic case concerning events at the police station and the TO building, and it's clear from your evidence that both those places are very close to each other, just across a small, narrow road. With a -- can you place a dot, a dot, in the part of the Bosanski Samac town where the TO and the -- the TO and the police station are located. You can't be precise, of course. It's not a highly detailed map. But the approximate area.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I can orientate myself pretty well. It's here on the corner. On the one side, you have the police station; and then on the other side of the road is the staff of the TO, Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: For the record, that looks like an "i" with a little dot at the top of it -- now a circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Now -- don't touch the screen anymore, if you don't mind. One more location in the town.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I would like to have the counsel's indulgence. If he can request the witness to remark the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- if he can mark it in red which is more visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Help us out, Mr. Tihic, could you just put a dot, a dot, in the location where the police station and the TO building are located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, inasmuch as I understand you were inviting him to mark something else, wouldn't it be more helpful if you use numbers; 1 for the first marking and 2 for the second?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I was going to -- I'm happy to do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: You heard the Bench's suggestion. Could you turn that into the number 1, please, a small 1.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: One. And then right below is 2. You just have to cross the road. It's on the very corner there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So 1 is the police station, and the number 2 represents the TO building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. And now, with a small number 3, could you please indicate the area of the town where the Mitar Trifunovic school is located.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you for doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, I seek to tender that image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked portion of 65 ter 10469 shall be given Exhibit P01545. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. I've finished with the map. And I'd now like another image or photograph to be placed on the screen if it could. Could 3419.47 please be put up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, counsel, can you please repeat the number again, please. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Yes, of course. It's an aerial photograph, and it's 3419.47.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, counsel, can you please indicate if that comes with a P prefix, or is that a 65 ter?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: My information is 3419.47. I can provide a hard copy, if that's of any use. Okay. That's the one, yep.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Is that Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, could you just circle two locations in that map, if you can. Firstly, the TO and the police station, and then the Mitar Trifunovic school. Do the police station and the TO building first, circle it, and mark it with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You've marked 1 and 2. Is 1 the police station and is 2 the TO building?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: And 3 is the school, the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I tender that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 -- the marked portion of 65 ter 3419.47 shall be given Exhibit P01546. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Incidentally, that's the Sava River there that you can see in that photograph and across the river is Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. You can see the Sava River and then on the other side is Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. I'd like to show you a building, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can the witness please be shown the photograph 65 ter 3419.50.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: When that has righted itself on the screen and you've had a chance to look at it, can you tell the Trial Chamber what that place is.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: This is the elementary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's the name of that place, that school?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Before the war, it was called Mitar Trifunovic, Uco.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And the places that, just moments ago, you've marked as the Mitar Trifunovic school, is that the school that you were talking about earlier?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I tender that image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P01547, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. I think that's all we need of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another image, 3419.51. What's the building in blue with a flag out the front?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: That's the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Now, you gave extensive evidence about your ordeal in the police station and the TO building in the Simic case. Is that the police station where you were from time to time beaten and interrogated?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is viewed from the street side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Right. Taken from the side where the TO building would be; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: All right. Okay. And if we can quickly show you one more image of the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: 3419.52, please. I should add that I will be seeking to tender both of these images.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I don't think there's any doubt about it; that's the same place, right, just taken directly from the front, the police station?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. Can we give them exhibit numbers before we proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 3419.51 shall be given Exhibit P01548, while 65 ter 3419.52 shall be given Exhibit P01549. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thanks. Next image: 3419.54, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's that place?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: That is the same building, the police station, but viewed from the courtyard, the police backyard, as it were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: It's the rear of the building, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If you just kept walking out from that back door, you'd eventually hit the Sava River, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. It would be a brief walk, some 50 to 100 metres, and then you would get to Sava River.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: In your evidence, you describe being imprisoned in that -- in that building. Is the window -- sorry, do any of those windows -- is the room where you were imprisoned in the police station depicted here in this photograph? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's the window with the bars with mesh. If you can see it, it's to the right side, right of the door. There were two cells there. They were 1 metre wide and perhaps 1.80 metres long. There were benches there. Nine of us sat and slept there. And I spent ten days there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you. And it's the only window that we can see with bars shown across it shown in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And if Your Honours please, I tender the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P01550. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And can -- one more: 3419.56, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Again, you can see that that's obviously the rear of the police station. Those garages that you can see there, were they there when you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were garages.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Do you know -- if you don't know, that's fine, but do you have any information as to whether anyone was ever held there or not during the time that you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I was not held there, but I know that other people were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And I tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P01551, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can we have 3419.57.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's the place that you can see in that photograph? You can see a white car and a little courtyard. What's in -- what building does the courtyard relate to?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: That courtyard is part of the building of -- where the Territorial Defence is located. On the right-hand side, you can see part of that building. But these -- this gate was closed off. You can see -- you see where this -- in the front part there was a shop, and in the back there were warehouses where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Okay. If you look at the photograph, if you were to enter that courtyard as you're looking at the photograph, were the men imprisoned in rooms on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the left-hand side. You can also see where the door is; that's where they were kept. And on the right-hand side, that building, that's where the offices of the Territorial Defence staff were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Could you just circle the door that led into the room where the prisoners were kept?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I tender that photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked portion of 65 ter 3419.57 shall be given Exhibit P01552, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: One more photograph, please, of this place: 3419.58.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The place with the two windows, is that the TO building office or headquarters?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I tender that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P01553, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'd like to show you another aerial shot, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Can the witness be shown 3419.48.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Have a look at that place at this road junction that you can see. Do you -- firstly, do you know what that area is from looking at it?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, this could be Crkvina. That is the junction where one road leads to Gracac, the other to Modrica. So this is Crkvina for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Focus your attention, please, on the building that you might say is smack-bang in the middle of the photograph. It's got a yard in front of it, and you can see little cars, two white cars and a blue car and then a little red car, right in the middle of the photograph. Do you see that? What's that place?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's the place where the prisoners were killed, the camp detainees, in May 1992. I mentioned earlier that incident. I wasn't there, myself, but I was told by other people who were there later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Killed by Lugar, Slobodan Miljkovic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, Slobodan Miljkovic, Lugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry for my mispronunciation. Circle the building, please, and then we'll tender that.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked portion of document 3419.48 shall be given Exhibit P01554.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the witness has marked it. I can't see it on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It had been marked. I was just about to ask whether that had been removed from the screen, because what now appears is not a marked copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, did we capture --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can confirm that we captured the marked portion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Thank you, I'm very grateful. And the last photograph I want to use is 3419.61.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: What's that place?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, that is the same place that we saw in the earlier photograph blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: The place at Crkvina?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is just a blow-up of that earlier photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Just for the purposes of the record, that's Crkvina, the place that you depicted in the previous aerial photograph?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: And in 1992, what was that place being used for, if you can tell us; if you don't know, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I know because the camp detainees who were kept there, they showed it to me, and this is where the crime was committed, when Slobodan Miljkovic, Lugar, killed some 16 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Was that place being used as a warehouse back in 1992, other than the purposes you've mentioned?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I mean, I think it used to be a warehouse.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, thank you very much for answering my questions again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio --

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, my mistake. I forgot to seek the production into evidence of that photo and I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P01555, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We have known each other since 2001. I don't know whether you recall the Samac case against Simic. Mr. Tihic, it is a fact, is it not, that the town of Bosanski Samac is of some strategic importance for Bosnia-Herzegovina; correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. The estuary of the Bosna River into the Sava River, the bridge itself, as well as certain mines.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I asked you about this because of an adjudicated fact, which is P95, which has to do with the strategic importance of Bosanski Samac from the military standpoint. Save for that aspect, it is geographically important for all of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the very reasons you have specified?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, geographically speaking and in terms of traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, is it not, that during 1991 there were weapons transport routes which, among others, included the routes from Croatia across the bridge in Bosanski Samac?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to say, but I think that most of the bridges were destroyed anyhow and there was only one left, although I cannot tell you what things eventually crossed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. We'll get back to that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P544 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: P1544.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the environs of Bosanski Samac. Could the usher be so kind as to help Mr. Tihic to have something marked in red on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, please put a number 1 next to the town of Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To the left-hand side and towards the middle of the page, we can see Modrica. Please write 2 next to it, if you can see it.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, in the upper right corner, there is Orasje, where I would kindly ask you to put a 3. Would you like them to zoom in?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't see it right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Orasje is right next to the Sava River.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. It is a fact that during 1992 this entire stretch shown on this map, on the left-hand side of the Bosna River, was under the control of the Croatian forces or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Odzak was for a while under their control, but not throughout 1992, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us approximately at what time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: In the first half of 1992 I presume.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please draw a line next to the Bosna River to mark the left side, the left bank, of the river which was under the control of Croatia -- of the Croatian forces.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think the territory surrounding Orasje in early 1992 was also controlled by the Croatian forces. Do you know approximately how the line ran?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: This is it more or less. From Grebnice to Orasje.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Across the Sava there's Croatia. We don't even need to say that it was, of course, controlled by the Croatian forces. Towards the bottom of the map, what was the territory controlled by the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? Can you tell us that, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I think we should go further down than what is shown on this map otherwise we can't see it at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So below the edge of the map at the bottom?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Under the Dayton Agreements, Orasje became a separate municipality in Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it had also been a separate municipality before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document with the markings made by Mr. Tihic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the marked portion of 65 ter 10470 shall be given Exhibit 1D00345. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, while we're still with this map, can you tell me this: It is a fact, is it not, that for the most of 1992 or let's say as of the beginning of the hostilities and until August or let's say summer of 1992, the road between Bosanski Samac and Modrica towards Doboj was cut off in the area of Modrica?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't think that road was cut off. In what period of time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: It depends what month we're talking about. Perhaps after April, by which time I had been detained. Before April, one could freely go to Sarajevo and back.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are aware of the fact that the road to Bijeljina was cut off at Brcko?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I -- I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I do realise that this happened after you were detained. Sir, you are probably aware that while you were in Bosanski Samac, from the area you indicated, from the area that was controlled by the Croatian forces, Bosanski Samac was shelled by artillery?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: While I was still free, it was not. Before the attack, Samac had not been shelled. I was detained after the attack, and at that time there were some military activities. There was probably mutual shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: However, during your detention in Bosanski Samac, which was the case for a while, you must have been able to hear artillery detonations?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I do not recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tihic, if I understand your testimony correctly, as of 1990 you have been a member of the SDA party; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After you became a member, you also became the president of the SDA in Bosanski Samac. When was that, approximately?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I think in September 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. When did you, Mr. Tihic, become a member of the Main Board of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: During the first party congress, which was held in 1990. I think it was in late November.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if you're moving on to something else, would this be a convenient point to take the break?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, before the witness enters the courtroom, am I right in thinking that there is, for the new material we discussed in the beginning of this session -- this hearing, there's no English translation for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: No, we've got an English translation, and that's been disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I found that after I found the B/C/S version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: -- or rather, following --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Will the Court have that today as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I can give that to -- how would you like it, Your Honours, electronically or hard copies? Whatever ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Whatever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: I'll make arrangements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be of assistance, it has been uploaded by our staff, so probably it's already in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, you told us that since 1990, that is, the first party congress, you were a member of the Main Board of the SDA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You certainly know Mr. Hasan Cengic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was he also a member of the Main Board, or what was his position in 1991 in the party, if you recall that?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: He was probably a member of the Main Board. He was one of the founders of the party. It is quite likely that he was a member of the Main Board, although I cannot recall that with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In any case, if our information is correct, he had his office in the party headquarters in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where his office was?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: He had a business of his own, and now he's a member of a -- of the party board which comprises some 100 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In 1991 was he an active member of the party in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: He was, although I don't recall his exact position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D180, which is an MFI document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm quite certain you can recognise Mr. Cengic's signature?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I really am not certain. I don't think I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have it in English, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this is the cover letter of a document issued by the SDA, at least that's what the cover letter looked like back in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Such memoranda always contained another sign which was the crescent moon, and I don't see it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise this as Mr. Cengic's signature?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the stamp?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, there were such stamps as this one. It says "SDA Sarajevo." It is possible that this is the stamp, although I don't know how exactly -- what exactly it looked like at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you recall, was the address of the party HQ was in Marsala Tita Street 7A?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And that is the address you can see in the top right-hand-side corner?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, and it still has offices there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, were you present at a meeting of the SDA on the 11th of June in the police hall in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: If you could enlighten me by the agenda, I might be able to answer that. I was at a meeting in the police hall, but I don't know whether it was on this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At that meeting, the Council of National Defence of the SDA was established?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please repeat the answer; we did not hear it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your previous answer because it was not recorded. My question was -- or actually, I was trying to jog your memory by saying that at that meeting of the 11th of June, the Council for National Defence of the SDA was established. What was your answer?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I was not present at that council session.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, it's not clear to me from the evidence, from questions or answers, what year we're talking about. I assume from the fact the document was dated 1991 that that's the year we're talking about, but it's not clear on the transcript to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're talking about 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, my question was whether you used this or similar type of memorandum -- or, rather, were you informed, by virtue of such a memorandum, of the establishment of such a council?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I know that we were notified that we had to have our security commissions within municipal party structures. This is what I am aware of. Whether it was written in this precise wording, that I don't know. But, in any case, I know we were busy establishing security commissions. Every municipal organisation within the party did so, and it is quite customary for all parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So do you recall having received this document or not?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, it is a fact that in the area of the municipality of Bosanski Samac members of the Croatian people were arming themselves quite intensively in 1991 and 1992?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: The fact is that the Serbs were arming themselves the most. They received their weapons from the JNA; and as for the others, upon having seen that the Serbs were arming themselves, they did the same in their own ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall that on the 26th of July, 1990, there was a religious ceremony held in Domaljevac on the occasion of the festivity of St. Anne. In particular, members of the HDZ rallied, and this was covered quite extensively?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I was an attorney-at-law at the time, and I had some of my clients in that village, so it is likely that I was in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that Croats were then putting forward the agenda that Croats should seize certain portions of Bosnia-Herzegovina and join with their motherland in order to have all the Croats in a single country?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I do not seem to recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that between the 1st and 3rd of February, 1992, a large amount of weapons arrived in the area of Odzak, whereupon it was distributed to the members of HDZ in the village of Prud?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that as early as August 1991 from Domaljevac there were more than 150 and 200 people from that village who were included in different paramilitary-type Croatian formations?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that on the 8th and the 9th of September, the HDZ of Bosanski Samac transferred weapons from the territory of Croatia into the village of Grebnice?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Just to make sure that there is no error in the transcript, religious ceremony you talked about in Domaljevac, the festivity of St. Anne, is that 1990, July 1990, or 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: July 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I will now show you a document, 1D03-1307. This is a regular report from the Croatian army command, Eastern Posavina Operational Group, of January 4th, 1992. It reads "Regular Report," and then, among other, there is an underlined portion where it says that certain dailies, including the Sarajevo "Oslobodjenje," and also the Sarajevo TV and radio reported the news that in the municipalities of Derventa, Bosanski Brod, and Odzak, around 1500 Croats have been armed, mostly with automatic rifles, light machine-guns, anti-aircraft guns, and anti-tank weapons. And in that context mention is made of some members, leading members, of the HDZ in various municipalities. And according to this information, the weapons in question arrived from the other side of the Sava, in other words, from Croatia. And it was also said that the army would take measures in order for these illegal weapons to be returned, and the dead-line of 48 hours was given. And since from this we can see that this was published and broadcast, published in Oslobodjenje and broadcast on Sarajevo TV and on the radio, I assume that you're aware of these?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, no, I don't. There were all sorts of information coming out, and they were really more like rumours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see here in the last sentence it says: "In that respect, the activities of the Croatian Democratic Union, or, rather, the leaders of the HDZ from these villages are asking the Main Staff of the Croatian army what they are to do if the army begins confiscating these weapons."

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't see that any mention here is made of Bosanski Samac. There's only mention of Derventa and Odzak.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, but that's all in the same area; right?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. I really can't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just pull it up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says -- or, rather, this document was signed by Lieutenant Ivo Petric, the OG deputy -- the OG --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- and it says that: "It is interesting to know that newspaper reports and the news carried by the television and radio in Sarajevo cited the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina as the source of this piece of information." Does this help refresh your memory?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, sir, you must know about the establishment of the Patriotic League and the Green Berets in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I heard about it, but I did not take any part in it. I heard about it after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to show you a document, 1D001 [as interpreted], dated November 16, 1990, entitled: "Preparations and Organisation of the Patriotic League to Defend the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." 1D00-0001. Do you know anything about this document? Have you ever received a document of this nature?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: No. Specifically, I don't know anything about this document, but I do know about the establishment of the Patriotic League and so on and so forth. I know that there were such instances where people organised themselves, because the -- all the military capabilities were on one side, so people organised themselves in order to defend themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now I would like to show you a document I'm sure you're familiar with. 1D03-4701. This is an SDA document, Bosanski Samac SDA. I don't have the date, but I imagine that you will remember this document. This document from the Party for Democratic Action of Bosanski Samac is entitled: "Organisation and Method of Receiving, Transmitting, and Conveying Orders for Mobilisation." There is a date appearing in the English version. I think it says the 21st of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, at that time, Samac had already been occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume that's the case. It should be -- the date should be earlier. But tell me, do you know anything about this document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I can't really remember. Can we see what's inside?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please -- can we please see the next page -- or, rather, the third page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this title is so pompous and pretentious.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you can see on this document where it says -- where your name appears as well. It says Sulejman Tihic and Alija Fitozovic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I cannot see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you recall the document now?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I don't remember this document, but I know that there was a commission which was busy working on these matters, and the objective was to try to prevent something, if that was possible at all, in view of our numbers, because we had a very small percentage of Muslims in Bosanski Samac. There is mention made of couriers, and the purpose was to see if we can set up a warning system so that we have time to move out on time and shelter ourselves. Now, we -- there were only about 7 per cent of Bosniaks in that town, and there were -- the largest number was Serb and then Croatians, so we had to do something.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you testified both in the Samac case and some other cases, and it is indisputable that you were at the head of a security commission or something to that effect of the party, and Alija Fitozovic, who was a retired soldier who had military experience, he was the commander of that same body?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was a reserve junior officer in Karlovac and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting, but the interpreters are asking that you speak directly into the microphone because they have a hard time hearing what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So Fitozovic was a reserve officer, officer in reserve, and therefore he had some military experience which qualified him for the suitable person to be the leader of that staff; correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was an officer in reserve or a junior officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this document, unlike what you told us a few moments ago, contains, on the following pages, on the next pages, it contains certain description of military formations and units.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page for the benefit of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says the engineering platoon and the commander was Atif Ratic. Do you know this man, Atif Ratic?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes, but that he was in charge of that platoon, I doubt it. I don't know where that came from. He was an inn keeper. I don't know what he was in the army. I don't even know if he served in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Could we see the page with the ERN Y027-4523. I'm told that this document was not uploaded as a complete document by some kind of error, so I will revisit it tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't even know if you should ask me about this document. Perhaps it would be a better idea to ask Mr. Fitozovic, because our documents stayed behind, and anyone could add whatever they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. But, in any case, it is a fact, isn't it, that at one point you established an armed unit composed of members of the Party of Democratic Action in Bosanski Samac; correct?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what you mean by "armed unit."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I will show you a document in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D00-2787. Can we have that, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this your signature on this document?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, do you know, whose signature this was?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't, but if you allow me to read, maybe I can deduce something from the content. But certainly this is not my signature. I know that some members of the SDA obtained weapons, that there was some -- there were some arms, and they were all to join the staff of Territorial Defence, because we were anxious about the possibility of these weapons being used in an uncontrolled way and then creating a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's analyse this document. It says the city command Bosanski Samac, it has a signature and a stamp of the democratic action party staff, and so on. So did the Party of Democratic Action have a city command or a town command?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: No. But the intention was that whoever had and possessed some weapons, that they should become members of the staff of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here it says that the staff of Territorial Defence was established according to the list enclosed, and your name appears on top of the list. Does that ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. If we can see the list, probably there was a list of all those who were prepared to join the staff of Territorial Defence thereby becoming part of the legal defence organs of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and it's possible that I'm on that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this your address, Vojvodjanskih Brigada 3? Was that your address at the time?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Yes. And now looking at this list, all of these people, the ranking members and the others, this is all a list of people who were prepared to place themselves under the control of the staff of Territorial Defence, or, rather, to join it, and a unit would be formed in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, it is not in dispute that these individuals who appear on this list possess -- had weapons; correct? You had a weapon, too.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I don't know if they all had a weapon. I don't know if every one of them had a weapon, but some of them did and I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Where are we going?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm just trying to explore, Your Honours, this document, whether I can refresh the memory of this witness, because I would like to tender this document in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: For what reason? I mean, what -- are we going in the direction of tu quoque?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, we are not going in the direction of tu quoque at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, this document shows 212 names. I suppose that you have been shown this document already in some of the earlier cases. Does this help jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that's a large number of names, and I don't really trust that that's a correct figure. Therefore, I don't even know if this document is authentic and whether it was in fact an attachment to the document that you've just shown me earlier, because I doubt that there were 200 people on a list of that sort. Maybe a shorter list, but not one numbering 200 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I propose we do this: I will ask my associates to make xeroxed copies of these documents, because we have to come back again tomorrow, and then perhaps you can take a look at those documents overnight and -- which might help refresh your memory, and then I will put some questions to you tomorrow about some of these documents.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, that's fine. But this first document, that was not my signature on it. And as for these lists, I don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's all right, Mr. Tihic. I will give you an opportunity to answer my questions relating to these documents that I will hand-over to you later this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, tell us, please, you know that the Assembly of the Serbian autonomous district was established on the 11th, in November 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's document P1353.18.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, could you please repeat your answer into the microphone because it wasn't recorded.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, I know that the Serbian autonomous region of northern Bosnia was established in November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let's try and put this in context. This happened after the Assembly session in -- of October 1991 where the declaration on an independent Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was adopted and where the Assembly -- deputies of the Serb Democratic Party walked out of the session; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't. But, yes, that was when it was established. This was the time when the Serbian autonomous districts were being established, and this began even earlier on, before this one for northern Bosnia. I can't recall the exact date. But this was in line with a policy whereby there were parallel government structures being established, parallel to the legal Government of Bosnia and Herzegovina. This was all illegal and unconstitutional.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- I can show you a document, if you have doubts about the date of this Assembly, that was on the 14th of October, 1991, where this declaration was adopted.

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: That's possible. I did not deny that, but I can't really recall the date myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For reference, may I just add that it's document 1392 -- 1D92.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D92.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you mentioned that this process of forming autonomous districts throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina was unconstitutional. Isn't it true, though, that the declaration of the Assembly of October 14th, whereby members of one ethnicity were practically disallowed to vote, that this, too, was unconstitutional?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: No, that's not true. This was a decision adopted by the Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the people of Bosnia and Herzegovina, where Bosniaks and Croats and Serbs voted. So it was legal -- constitution. But here, mention is made, and it's only the establishment of a Serbian autonomous district of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this is unique in the world where in a state only one people would establish their own districts. That's impossible. That's unconstitutional totally because there are three peoples there, three ethnicities, and it's -- this is completely unreasonable.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, did you know that the SDA in Banja Luka made a statutory decision insisting on the establishment of a certain municipality called Stari Grad?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It is possible, but I wasn't sufficiently senior within the party to be -- know -- to know of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 1D4.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in the municipality of Kljuc at a session of the Club of Deputies of the SDA and the MBO the new municipality of Bosanski Kljuc was established?

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that. I don't know why it was necessary. It was not our policy to create new municipalities, and I highly doubt this. Besides, Kljuc was populated by Bosniaks mostly, so why ask for a new municipality?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is dated the 30th of January, 1992. I'm referring to a report about the meeting. It is 1D03-4707. Have a look. It says Bosanski Kljuc municipality. It says: "At yesterday's session of the SDA ..."

utterances.speaker: SULEJMAN TIHIC
utterances.text: This is quite a strange body of text. There's no heading, no paragraphs. I don't know who did this; and if they did, it doesn't seem right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: If this is not tu quoque against the witness's opinion that the creation of Serb autonomous regions was unconstitutional, what is it then?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I would gladly explain, but maybe the witness should be excused in that case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Could the usher please escort the witness out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness asserts that the establishment of the Serb autonomous districts was unconstitutional and illegal. It is our assertion, which the witness denies, is that it was a reaction to the unconstitutional and illegal decision that had been made by the Assembly. It is a fact and we are trying to prove that all parties, that is to say the Muslims, Croats, and Serbs, created their own autonomous regions and their own municipalities in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1991 and 1992. I intend to show to the witness an instruction. For your reference, it is 1D3. It is an instruction of the SDA on how to divide municipalities up. A local commune where Bosniaks were in the majority would separate from the rest of its municipalities. This was no policy or no decision of the Serbs to create their respective autonomous regions. This was simply a fact of reality which reflected what the other peoples in Bosnia-Herzegovina did. All the peoples in Bosnia made such statutory decisions about the way the republic should be organised. In this case, it is certainly not a tu quoque approach of this Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: While we're at it, Mr. Zecevic, you said - where is it? - that about the Assembly of October 14th you said that members of one ethnicity were practically disallowed to vote. Are you referring to the fact that the Serb delegates left the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The situation, Your Honours, was the following: The president of the Assembly declared that the Assembly session was over because of the certain dispute between the delegates. After that, the delegates of the Serbian Democratic Party left the parliament. And after they left the parliament it was unconstitutionally and not in accordance with the law, the session was reopened, and the decision on declaration of the independent Bosnia and Herzegovina has been brought -- brought up. And we will -- we definitely intend in our Defence case to prove that beyond a reasonable doubt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, unless we -- the three of us have wholly missed the point, accepting -- taking on board everything you have just said, where does this then take us, having regard to the indictment, which, of course, is what we are about in terms of this trial, both what the Prosecution proves and what you are defending against?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm just briefly covering the general context, and I am about to move into the area which is directly connected to our indictment, namely, the role of the MUP, the Republika Srpska, the Crisis Staffs, and et cetera, and the crimes committed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. You can move directly there, can't you? The background is -- there's no real dispute in terms of the course of events and the legislative goings-on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid that I must disagree. I think there is a -- there is a deep dispute between the parties, on that part of the general context. And, Your Honours, I wanted to use the witness because I assumed he, as a lawyer, the intellectual, the president of the SDA, and the member of the Main Board of the SDA since 1990, to be able to give us some of the documents which we didn't -- which we didn't introduce through other witnesses which were not in a position to comment that -- on that. I tried with the witness, but he didn't -- he was unable to comment on these documents as well. So that is the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI FAZIO
utterances.text: If Your Honours please, the fact that it is tu quoque is really eloquently set out by Mr. Zecevic's own words. "It's a fact that we're trying to prove that all parties, that is to say, Muslims and Croats and Serbs, created their own autonomous regions and their own municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1991 and 1992." And if you look at the previous cross-examination that preceded that on the issue of arms and arming, we never got to any point beyond evidence establishing or trying to establish that Muslims were arming themselves in Bosanski Samac. Same is occurring here now with regard to the creation of these autonomous regions and self-governing regions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a suggestion to make. I think maybe it would be the best -- the best that we adjourn for the day now and continue tomorrow. I believe I have one and a half hours more with the witness, and that would be something -- the area that I'm going to cover is going to be much more related to the indictment directly, as I understand the Trial Chamber would appreciate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, we agree with your suggestion, that your cross-examination be suspended at this point. But before we take a decision as to whether to adjourn, we'll inquire as to whether counsel for - thank you - counsel for Mr. Zupljanin would wish to use such of today as can be practically used.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic -- Mr. Krgovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We don't have cross-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Pardon me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: We don't have cross-examination for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. Could we have the witness back into the court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Tihic, we have invited you back into the courtroom in order to formally take the adjournment. We are about to rise for the day, and I'm obliged to caution you that having been sworn as a witness you cannot have any communication with counsel from either side. And in such conversation as you may have with anyone outside of the courtroom, you cannot discuss your testimony. So we will take the adjournment now until 9.00 tomorrow morning in this courtroom -- I believe we're in this courtroom. Courtroom II, I'm sorry, Courtroom II tomorrow, at which point Mr. Zecevic will conclude his cross-examination which he estimates would be for another 90 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
